An effective Cybersecurity Plan was documented based on the inventory of attack surfaces which can be exploited on our project. An organization’s attack surface includes the many vulnerabilities, pathways, or methods (i.e., attack vectors) that threat actors can use to gain unauthorized access to the network or sensitive data, or to carry out a cyberattack. For example, the inventory of attack surfaces for our project includes integrations between IT systems as well as physical devices (e.g., EV chargers.) 12 6.1.3.1 Subtask 3.1.0: Develop Cybersecurity Plan The Cybersecurity Plan was first completed and submitted on August 31, 2023. The plan was developed after conducting in-depth discussions to document the detailed system architecture. By first developing a common understanding of the system architecture for the project, the attack surfaces for the project became readily apparent. Based on the documented system architecture for the project, the project team was able to document and submit an effective first version of the Cybersecurity Plan. Since August 2023, the project has gained additional insights into the interfaces, systems, and physical hardware needed to implement the project. For example, the project team gained significant insights as part of the negotiations with OSI regarding the integrations with OSI Integra DERMS. Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) also provided additional feedback and comments on the first version of the Cybersecurity Plan. Based on this new information, the project team submitted an updated Cybersecurity Plan on February 29, 2024. The cybersecurity framework and plan were implemented at the USU microgrid facility as part of the Budget Period 2 activities. In September 2025, PacifiCorp also conducted a 3rd party penetration test for all project systems within the utility ecosystem. No immediate concerns were raised during the audit, but the final report was not yet shared at the time of project termination. The Cybersecurity Plan was viewed as a living document that was updated at least every six months. The project team completed the Phase A and Phase B cybersecurity checklists from PNNL’s cyber team and was working on completing the Phase C checklist when the project was terminated. 6.1.3.2 Subtask 3.2.0: Identify Cybersecurity Framework to Address Risks The project team identified cybersecurity risks across the project sites, both internal and external, and developed a cybersecurity framework that would have led to the development of multiple tools for defense, detection, and mitigation of cybersecurity threats in the project. 6.1.4 Task 4: Develop Business Model Plan In light of the significant transformations within the energy sector, driven by the swift adoption of DERs and regulatory changes such as FERC Order 2222, the plan for a business model that leverages DERs for grid services for aggregation and deployment at the wholesale market level is much needed. By advocating for this strategic redirection, the plan positioned utilities to navigate and grow in the changing energy landscape, leveraging opportunities for revenue generation through firm capacity, operating reserves, and the provision of energy.
